handback.t:
W3 (MEMORY-BYTES) round 3: `CompactRouter` is built, and in my five synthetic worlds it is certified equivalent to the f64 recommended router and no slower. That includes the 32-agent case round 2 left inconclusive. All 228 lib tests pass, 11 of them new. I did not commit anything.

**What was built** (`src/compact.rs`, new, opt-in)
- `CompactRouter` implements `Router` with the same decision rule as `defaults::recommended_router`. Only the state encoding differs: one sparse row per feature, u16 weights, Q16 counts (1/1024 units), and interned ids (private or `SharedVocab`) or 32-bit hash ids.
- It supports serde save/load, exact byte accounting via `bytes()`, and `fork_blank()` for many brains over one shared vocab and keyword table.
- The generic core also provides `CompactRouterF32` and `CompactRouterF64`. The f64 instance is decision- and rng-identical to the shipped router, shown by a unit test and by a diff of exactly 0 in every world and seed. So any u16 difference is representation error, not logic.
- Limits, enforced by the constructor: at most 64 agents, plain Hebbian rule only, fixed agent count. A tuned `HebbianConfig` with the meta, weighting, ucb or agg options on is rejected by `CompactConfig::from_configs`.

**Repo edits outside my files**
- One line, `pub mod compact;`, appended to `src/lib.rs`.
- The `g3_common` worlds and stats are a snapshot of `f3_common` plus TOST helpers.

**Equivalence**
- Protocol, declared in the `g3_equiv.rs` header before running: paired by seed on mean expected success, ±0.005 margin, TOST at α=.05 (the 90% CI inside the margin), Holm over the 5 worlds. Nothing was tuned; the config is the recommended one.
- Primary split is pooled seeds 31-90 (60 seeds). All five worlds are certified; diff is compact minus f64:

| World | Diff | 90% CI | 95% CI | Holm p |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| sim-fixed | −0.0001 | [−0.0003, +0.0001] | [−0.0003, +0.0001] | .0000 |
| sim-random | +0.0004 | [−0.0007, +0.0015] | [−0.0010, +0.0017] | .0000 |
| sim-no-traps | +0.0001 | [−0.0001, +0.0004] | [−0.0001, +0.0004] | .0000 |
| big-32agents | +0.0005 | [−0.0023, +0.0033] | [−0.0028, +0.0038] | .0046 |
| big-32agents-longtail | +0.0003 | [−0.0013, +0.0019] | [−0.0016, +0.0022] | .0000 |

- The frozen confirm split 61-90 certifies all five worlds at ±0.005. The held split 31-60 does too, but big-32agents only just (Holm p=.039).
- The fresh power split 91-250 (160 seeds) certifies all five at ±0.005 and at ±0.003. The ±0.003 certification is borderline: Holm p=.045 for big-32agents and for the long-tail world.
- The f32 and hash32 variants behave the same: f32 has diff exactly 0 everywhere, and hash32 equals table mode because no hash collisions occurred in these worlds.

**Memory and speed**
- Method: bytes come from a counting allocator (live bytes of K independently trained brains per world). ns is the min over 31 interleaved repetitions of route plus feedback.

| World | f64 bytes/brain | Compact private | Compact shared vocab | Agents/GiB (f64 → private \| shared) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| sim 6 agents | 16.1 KB | 5.7 KB (2.8×) | 2.4 KB (6.7×) | 66.8k → 189k \| 449k |
| big-32agents | 246 KB | 44.7 KB (5.5×) | 20.9 KB (11.8×) | 4.4k → 24.0k \| 51.5k |
| long-tail (1838 features) | 1.88 MB | 251 KB (7.5×) | 75.9 KB (24.7×) | 572 → 4.3k \| 14.1k |

- Latency (ns, min fresh): ref 1180 → 601 (sim-fixed), 3477 → 1265 (big-32agents), 4721 → 1302 (long-tail). The ratio is 0.28–0.51 across worlds, against a declared limit of +10%.
- Allocations per decision drop from 12–15 to 0.
- The sim rows are the figures for sim-fixed; sim-random and sim-no-traps are within a few percent.

**Negatives** (more in the board entry)
- The box was 50–81% busy during the full perf run. Absolute ns are noisy (±30%); only the interleaved ratios mean anything. A quiet-ish quick run (41–48% busy) gave 0.33–0.51, the same picture.
- At 30 seeds the 32-agent worlds only just certify at ±0.005 and cannot certify ±0.003. At the 8-seed smoke run 4 of 5 worlds are inconclusive.
- The shared-vocab numbers hold only when many brains share one vocabulary. A self-contained brain, which is what save/load gives, is 2.8×–7.5× smaller.
- Sparse rows lose to dense rows at 6 agents. The library type gives 449k agents/GiB where f3's bin-local dense layout got 526k.
- The vocabulary is unbounded for open token streams. The JSON state is text and larger than the in-memory brain (4 KB, 35 KB and 124 KB). The commit-charge column in the perf JSON is unreliable.
- Worlds and metric (expected success) are mine and synthetic.
- One foreground `cargo test --lib` stalled for 30 minutes with the test exe spinning, on a box where others were editing `serve.rs` and `spatial.rs`. After I killed it, a fresh build ran green in about 1 s and three reruns were green. I could not trace the cause; it is worth one rerun by the director.

**Rerun** (exact commands are in the board entry)
- `cargo test --release --offline --lib compact`
- `cargo run --release --offline --bin g3_equiv` (~11 s, deterministic)
- `cargo run --release --offline --bin g3_perf` (~5.5 min)
